lines.text: This guy bought a brand new car, just to sit next to his neighbour at every red light.
Every morning, Rohan and Arjun leave the same colony, at the same time, in two different cars.
First signal, they wave.
Second signal, thumbs up.
Fifth signal, they've run out of greetings.
This went on for two years.
One day, Rohan rolls down the window,
bro, where do you even work?
Same office.
Same floor.
Same team.
Same meetings. Two years. Cameras off.
So they made a carpool group.
Sixty messages later, nobody knew who was driving, and Sharma ji's two minutes had become forty.
Group, dead. Four cars again.
Turns out, carpools never fail because of the car.
They fail because of the planning.
So they let an app do the boring part.
A roster picks today's driver. One tap says you're ready. And everyone watches the car arrive. Live.
Now it's one car, four friends, and three very bored parking spots.
Sharma ji is still late though. But now, everyone can see exactly where.
If you wave at your neighbour every morning, the app's called Sahyatri.
Check it out. Link in bio.
